title: Data Loading — Data Loader Interface — Conversion to Standard B with Solid State Media

ata.title: Data Loading — Portable Data Loader Interface

abstract: Conversion of the data loader interface to standard B, replacing the obsolete media reader with solid state media and adding a configuration report that names every load actually written to the aircraft.

sections.planning_reason: The original media has been out of production since 2019 and operators are buying it second hand, which the spares organisation cannot support beyond a two year forward cover. Separately, the interface produces no record of what was loaded, so a configuration dispute after a software load can only be settled by reading every target computer individually, which on the current build standard means eleven readings. Twenty-two operators listed the media obsolescence among their top ten fleet issues in the 2019 survey.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin converts the interface to standard B. The aircraft-side transceiver is retained and the media side is replaced by a solid state reader inside the unit. A configuration report is written to the maintenance system after every load, naming the target, the part number written and the result. The rack receives a revised air baffle so that cooling no longer depends on the blanking plate above the unit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: De-power the avionics rack and confirm that no load is in progress. Get access to the avionics bay in zones 252 and 264. Remove the unit from the rack position at FIN 78TN. Install the air baffle in the rack at FIN 23TN and secure the internal harness with the loop clamps LN760453-5C. Install the standard B unit built around the transceiver D4545112932616. Restore power and do a test load to a non-critical target following task AMM-Z-45-45-11-900-026-A. Confirm that the configuration report appears in the maintenance system and that it names the target and the part number written. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft already at the extended temperature transceiver standard. Aircraft that never had that change must embody it first, or the standard B unit will inherit the temperature limitation from the rack cooling arrangement.
sections.material_note: Kit K4545-1016-01 contains the standard B unit, the air baffle and the clamp set for one aircraft. The unit is a twenty week item. Removed standard A units are returned to Aeralis and are converted through the repair loop.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin. Operators dependent on the original media are advised to embody within 24 months.

ata.title: Data Loading — Portable Data Loader Interface

abstract: Conversion of the data loader interface to standard B with solid state media and a configuration report, re-issued to make the rack air baffle a permanent part of the installation rather than a piece of kit content.

sections.planning_reason: The original media has been out of production since 2019 and operators are buying it second hand, which the spares organisation cannot support beyond a two year forward cover. Separately, the interface produces no record of what was loaded, so a configuration dispute after a software load can only be settled by reading every target computer individually, which on the current build standard means eleven readings. Twenty-two operators listed the media obsolescence among their top ten fleet issues in the 2019 survey.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin converts the interface to standard B. The aircraft-side transceiver is retained and the media side is replaced by a solid state reader inside the unit. A configuration report is written to the maintenance system after every load, naming the target, the part number written and the result. The rack receives a revised air baffle so that cooling no longer depends on the blanking plate above the unit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: De-power the avionics rack and confirm that no load is in progress. Get access to the avionics bay in zones 252 and 264. Remove the unit from the rack position at FIN 78TN. Install the air baffle in the rack at FIN 23TN and secure the internal harness with the loop clamps LN760453-5C. The baffle is part of the aircraft configuration and not a kit consumable: it stays in the rack at every later unit change and is recorded on the aircraft configuration sheet at embodiment. Install the standard B unit built around the transceiver D4545112932616. Restore power and do a test load to a non-critical target following task AMM-Z-45-45-11-900-026-A. Confirm that the configuration report appears in the maintenance system and that it names the target and the part number written. Record the embodiment and the baffle installation.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft already at the extended temperature transceiver standard. Aircraft that never had that change must embody it first, or the standard B unit will inherit the temperature limitation from the rack cooling arrangement.
sections.material_note: Kit K4545-1016-01 contains the standard B unit, the air baffle and the clamp set for one aircraft. The unit is a twenty week item. Removed standard A units are returned to Aeralis and are converted through the repair loop. The baffle is not returned with the unit and is not re-ordered at a later unit change: once installed it is what keeps the rack thermally correct, because the cooling path no longer depends on the blanking plate above the unit, and any later interface standard must call the baffle up explicitly in its own kit list rather than assume it is present.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin. Operators dependent on the original media are advised to embody within 24 months.

revision_history.reason: Rack air baffle declared part of the aircraft configuration and required to be called up explicitly by later interface standards
